nodes.content: Develop a legged locomotion controller that identifies hidden terrain yielding limits while maintaining recoverability during exploratory foot contacts.
requirements: Estimate previously unseen terrain’s load-bearing limits with median relative error below 15%.
Reduce falls by 30% versus an otherwise matched nonexploratory controller at equal traversal speed.

nodes.content: Combine bounded force-ramp foot probes and Bayesian yield-threshold inference with chance-constrained MPC preserving a verified recovery foothold.
How should probe force ramps balance yield-threshold information against the probability of losing a recoverable stance?
With ≤1% predicted stance-loss risk, entropy-maximizing ramps achieve <15% median yield error and ≥30% fewer falls versus speed-matched nonexploratory control.
Calibrate force–sinkage posteriors, optimize ≤1%-risk probe ramps, then benchmark yield error and falls on held-out substrates against speed-matched controls.
Run 300 instrumented foot-ramp contacts across sand, peat, and loam to calibrate Bayesian yield-threshold posteriors.
FootRamp-300: a labeled force–sinkage dataset and calibrated Bayesian yield-threshold posterior for sand, peat, and loam.
Using FootRamp-300 posteriors, benchmark entropy-ramp yield error, calibration, ≤1% stance-loss risk, and speed-matched falls versus nonexploratory control.
Across 500 held-out crossings per arm, median yield error was 12.8%, stance-loss 0.8%, and falls 5.2% versus 8.0% speed-matched.
Field-test FootRamp-300-initialized entropy ramps on unseen mud and clay against speed-matched controls; measure yield error, stance-loss, and falls.
Across 250 unseen mud/clay crossings per arm, median yield error was 22%, stance-loss 2.4%, and falls 11.2% versus 13.6% speed-matched.
Do delayed sinkage and hysteresis in mud and clay cause overconfident yield estimates and unsafe probe ramps?
Online hysteresis-aware sinkage inference restores <15% yield error, ≤1% stance loss, and ≥30% fewer speed-matched falls on mud/clay.
Fit hysteretic delayed-sinkage dynamics, recalibrate probe-risk bounds online, then retest on new mud/clay crossings against speed-matched controls.
Initialize hysteretic filter from FootRamp-300; test 400 unseen mud/clay crossings per speed-matched arm for yield error, stance loss, and falls.
Across 400 mud/clay crossings per arm, median yield error was 18.1%, stance-loss 1.5%, and falls 10.0% versus 13.0% speed-matched.
With FootRamp-300-initialized hysteretic filtering, run 200 slow-draining clay crossings per arm, measuring lag-stratified yield error, stance-loss, and speed-matched falls.
Across 200 slow-draining clay crossings per arm: median yield error 13.4%, stance loss 0.5%, falls 6% versus 9% speed-matched.
Does variable mud drainage, rather than delayed clay sinkage, explain the remaining yield errors and stance-loss violations?
Adding drainage-state inference to hysteretic filtering yields <15% mud/clay median error, ≤1% stance loss, and ≥30% fewer speed-matched falls.
Stratify mud by drainage time; fit drainage-state filtering; measure yield error, stance loss, and falls versus speed-matched baselines.
Benchmark a FootRamp-300-initialized hysteretic drainage-state filter across 400 drainage-stratified mud/clay crossings per arm: yield error, stance loss, speed-matched falls.
Across 400 crossings per arm, drainage-state filtering achieved 13.9% median yield error, 0.75% stance loss, and 7.5% falls versus 11%.
Select drainage-state filtering: mixed-terrain yield error 13.9%, stance loss 0.75%, fall reduction 31.8%; hysteresis-only failed despite slow-clay success.
Probe terrain with progressive vertical load cycles; estimate yield from residual sinkage and preserve recovery through viability-kernel foothold selection.
Can residual sinkage from progressive load cycles identify yield before probing eliminates viable recovery footholds?
On unseen substrates, viability-gated load cycles achieve <15% median yield error and ≥30% fewer falls versus speed-matched nonexploratory control.
Calibrate residual-sinkage yield estimates, compute foothold viability kernels, then compare speed-matched traversal outcomes on withheld substrates.
Run 300 unseen-silt crossings per arm; measure viability-gated cycling’s yield error and falls against speed-matched nonexploratory control.
Across 300 unseen-silt crossings per arm, median yield error was 13.1%; falls were 6% versus 9% speed-matched.
Estimate yield force from graded, variable-area sole preloads while capture-region MPC preserves three verified stance contacts.
Can changing sole contact area disambiguate pressure-dependent terrain yield from transient sinkage without sacrificing capture-region feasibility?
Alternate toe and full-sole preloads on held-out terrains; fit pressure–sinkage curves and compare yield error, capture feasibility, and speed-matched falls.
Run 240 held-out gravel-over-mud crossings per arm, alternating toe/full-sole preloads; log yield error, three-contact capture feasibility, and falls.
On gravel-over-mud (240/arm), yield error was 21%, capture feasibility 86%, and falls 13% versus 10% speed-matched.
Can capture-region MPC detect when three stance contacts cannot arrest a slip triggered by toe preloads on layered terrain?
A slip-aware capture-region forecast flags ≥90% of unrecoverable toe-preload slips ≥100 ms early, with ≤10% false alarms.
Train slip-aware capture forecasts on toe-preload trajectories, then score early detection and false alarms on withheld layered-terrain crossings.
Replay 180 withheld gravel-over-mud toe-preload trajectories; score capture forecasts ≥100 ms before unrecoverable slip and false alarms.
On 180 withheld trajectories, slip-aware forecasts flagged 92% of unrecoverable slips ≥100 ms early, with 8% false alarms.
Test frozen slip-aware forecasts on 250 live wet gravel-over-mud toe-preload crossings; measure ≥100-ms unrecoverable-slip recall and false-alarm rate.
In 250 live wet crossings, forecasts flagged 71% of unrecoverable slips ≥100 ms early, with 17% false alarms.
Does moisture-dependent friction shorten toe-preload slip warning times enough to invalidate replay-trained capture forecasts?
Online friction-adaptive capture forecasts restore ≥90% unrecoverable-slip detection ≥100 ms early with ≤10% false alarms in wet crossings.
Estimate friction from stance micro-slips, adapt capture forecasts online, and compare wet-terrain early-slip recall and false alarms against frozen forecasts.
Run 300 wet gravel-over-mud crossings with micro-slip friction adaptation; compare ≥100-ms slip recall and false alarms against frozen forecasts.
Across 300 wet crossings, frozen low-moisture forecasts reached 92% ≥100-ms slip recall/8% false alarms; adaptation overall reached 85%/12%.
Stratify 300 new wet gravel-over-mud crossings by measured friction; compare adaptive and frozen ≥100-ms slip recall and false alarms.
In 120 low-friction wet crossings, adaptive forecasts achieved 92% ≥100-ms slip recall and 9% false alarms versus frozen 69%/18%.
Reject layered-terrain variable-area probing after 21% yield error and excess falls; retain friction-adaptive slip alerts only for low-friction conditions.
Use bounded stance-foot impedance chirps and tactile shear imaging to infer yield force while reachability-shielded MPC reserves emergency touchdown.
Can shear-imaged impedance chirps distinguish impending substrate yield from reversible deformation before emergency touchdown becomes unreachable?
Shear-imaged chirps yield <15% median limit error and ≥30% fewer speed-matched falls while touchdown reachability remains ≥99%.
Calibrate chirp shear features against yield loads, shield probes with touchdown reachability, then compare held-out traversal error and falls.
Record 360 chirped contacts on peat, loam, and mud; label first irreversible sinkage using force plates and tactile shear frames.
ShearChirp-360 pairs tactile shear sequences, chirp forces, and first-irreversible-sinkage yield labels for peat, loam, and mud.
Using ShearChirp-360 labels, benchmark held-out median yield error, emergency-touchdown reachability, and speed-matched falls against nonexploratory control.
Across 300 held-out crossings per arm, median yield error was 12.6%, touchdown reachability 99.3%, and falls 5.7% versus 8.4%.
Field-test ShearChirp-360-trained chirps on 250 unseen waterlogged-silt crossings per arm; measure yield error, touchdown reachability, and speed-matched falls.
On 250 unseen waterlogged-silt crossings per arm, median yield error was 19.4%, touchdown reachability 96.8%, and falls 10.8% versus 12.4%.
Does waterlogged silt’s rate-dependent pore-pressure response distort shear-chirp yield estimates and invalidate precomputed touchdown reachability?
Online pore-pressure inference and drainage-aware reachability achieve <15% median yield error, ≥99% touchdown reachability, and ≥30% fall reduction on silt.
Fit pore-pressure dynamics from chirp phase lag, update drainage-conditioned touchdown sets, then benchmark unseen silt against speed-matched baselines.
Using ShearChirp-360, compare original and pore-pressure-adaptive chirps across 300 unseen-silt crossings per arm: yield error, touchdown reachability, speed-matched falls.
On unseen silt (300/arm), original/adaptive yield error: 19.1%/13.2%; touchdown reachability: 97.0%/99.3%; adapted falls: 7% versus 11% speed-matched.
Stress-test ShearChirp-360-initialized adaptive chirps on 300 variable-drainage silt crossings per arm; record yield error, touchdown reachability, speed-matched falls.
On variable-drainage silt (300/arm), median yield error was 16.8%, touchdown reachability 98.3%, and falls 9% versus 12% speed-matched.
Do within-stance drainage transitions outpace pore-pressure updates, causing missed yield onset and overestimated touchdown reachability?
A 20-ms change-point pore-pressure filter restores <15% yield error, ≥99% touchdown reachability, and ≥30% fall reduction on variable-drainage silt.
Detect within-stance drainage change points from chirp phase shifts, recompute touchdown sets every 20 ms, and benchmark silt traversals.
Using ShearChirp-360, compare pore-pressure and 20-ms change-point filters across 300 variable-drainage silt crossings per arm: yield error, reachability, speed-matched falls.
Across 300 crossings per arm, pore-pressure filtering met all targets on slow-transition silt; change-point filtering missed all three overall.
Using ShearChirp-360, test 20-ms change-point filtering on 240 rapid-drainage-transition silt crossings per arm; record yield error, reachability, speed-matched falls.
On rapid-transition silt (240/arm), change-point filtering achieved 13.7% median yield error, 99.2% touchdown reachability, and 18 versus 27 falls.
Retain baseline chirps off silt; select pore-pressure filtering for stable drainage or change-point filtering for rapid transitions, pending validation.
